name: Fleet Biplane Trainers (Models 1/2/7/16)
summary: Compact two-seat primary-training biplane of the late 1920s and 1930s, used by civil flight schools and several air forces and still flown by antiquers.

wings: Fabric-covered wings with wood spars and rounded tips
engines: Small radial engine (Kinner, Warner or similar), usually uncowled or with a ring cowl

tellTales: Compact open-cockpit tandem biplane with a small radial engine
Equal-span staggered wings with a single bay
Uncowled radial with exposed cylinders on a small, light airframe

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stearman is much larger and heavier with a big radial engine; the Fleet is a small, light, small-radial biplane.
The two are alike in size and layout; the Fleet Models 2 and 7 have a distinctive looped radius rod on the port main gear leg.
The Meyers OTW is a later design with a more streamlined, compact look; the Fleet is a plainer 1920s-30s trainer.
